A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same NeUQI study and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Renumbered material, including Full Results moving from Appendix G to H, can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v3 reports original LLaMA and Qwen quantization experiments, including perplexity, benchmark accuracy, runtime measurements, and ablations in Section 5 and the appendices.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experiments and adds initialization controls, QuIP integration results, and further baseline measurements.

M1.justification: The quantization objective, floating-point zero-point optimization, transition-point reduction, coarse-to-fine scale search, and Algorithms 1–4 remain unchanged. The new QuIP experiment applies the existing initialization without documenting a revised NeUQI procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use C4, WikiText2, ARC-Easy, ARC-Challenge, PIQA, HellaSwag, and WinoGrande with the same model families. The additional comparisons retain existing data and task coverage.

E2.justification: v4 adds MSE initialization in Table 4, EfficientQAT '+Floating z' in Table 7, and QuIP versus QuIP+NeUQI in Table 11. Tables 13–16 substantially expand the existing 3/4-bit appendix comparisons with GPTAQ and MagR, beyond v3's GPTQ–NeUQI tables.

E3.justification: Table 7 introduces a floating-zero-point control within the existing 2-bit, group-size-128 evaluation. Existing calibration sample counts, context lengths, distillation budgets, metrics, and quantization settings remain unchanged; the PDFs do not establish rerunning the retained experiments.

E4.justification: v4 extends the initialization analysis with MSE and adds a floating-zero-point control to distinguish its effect from NeUQI initialization. Appendix G additionally tests NeUQI's benefit within QuIP after distribution-smoothing transformations. Existing search, Hadamard-transform, and scale-freezing analyses remain.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without introducing repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Additional result rows do not change the uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Retained numerical results are unchanged, but v4 substantially expands baseline and control results. New Table 11 reports LLaMA 2 7B C4 perplexity of 110.38 for QuIP versus 16.98 for QuIP+NeUQI. Added competitors also change rankings: in Table 14, MagR's accuracy of 72.38 exceeds NeUQI's retained 72.19 for LLaMA 3 70B at 3 bits with group size 128.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, loss derivations, complexity arguments, Lemma B.1 and its proof, and appendix algorithms are retained. No substantive changes to assumptions or mathematical reasoning were found.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the claims about Min-Max constraints, efficient near-optimal initialization, low-bit performance, and compatibility with transformations and fine-tuning. The additional experiments support these existing claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: Appendix G explicitly interprets the QuIP results as showing initialization remains important after weight-distribution smoothing. Table 13 newly acknowledges withholding the LLaMA 2 13B, 3-bit/group-128 MagR result because it is anomalous and deviates from the expected trend.

D1.justification: Section 5.4 adds a footnote identifying and linking the specific legacy MSE grid-search implementation in the GPTQ repository. Existing implementation, hardware, calibration, optimization, and evaluation details in Appendices D–F remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive related-work positioning remain the same; QuIP was already discussed and cited in v3. Updates to the GPT3.int8 and WinoGrande reference entries are bibliographic changes.

P1.justification: v4 adds acknowledgements and a short QuIP appendix, updates correspondence and publication text, and adjusts baseline wording and cross-references. Full Results becomes Appendix H. Most scientific prose and the main narrative structure remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v4 adds the QuIP table, expands Tables 4 and 7 and the higher-bit result tables, and splits the former Qwen table into Tables 15–16. These additions cause localized layout changes; Figure 1 and the established table and document styles are retained.

improvement.justification: Compared with v3's narrower higher-bit tables, v4's GPTAQ/MagR comparisons and additional initialization controls make the empirical case more informative. The QuIP experiment adds direct compatibility evidence. These gains strengthen existing conclusions, but sparse explanation of the floating-zero-point control and Table 13's exclusion of an anomalous MagR result solely for deviating from the expected trend limit the improvement.
